system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: In the prompts, we set some injectable slots such as {{ Demonstrations }} and {{ Candidate Models }}. These slots are uniformly replaced with the corresponding text before being fed into the LLM.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: To assist with task planning, the chat history is available as {{ Chat Logs }}, where you can trace the user-mentioned resources
env_context_strategy.note: No repository/environment context; only user request and chat logs.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: Token Lengths is another common problem when using LLM, since the maximum token length is always limited.
context_compaction.note: Paper notes token-length limits as an unsolved problem; no compaction mechanism described. Candidate models are top-K filtered, but that is prompt construction, not history compaction.

observation_format.evidence_quote: These inference results are presented in a structured format, such as bounding boxes with detection probabilities in the object detection model, answer distributions in the question-answering model

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: generating a list of tasks with the following format: [{"task": task, "id", task_id, "dep": dependency_task_ids, "args": {"text": text, "image": URL, "audio": URL, "video": URL}}]

tool_count.note: Tools are Hugging Face models selected per task type; no fixed tool schema count given.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: The task must be selected from the following options: {{ Available Task List }}.
edit_primitive.note: Actions are ML model invocations; no file-editing tool.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: {"model_id": model id #1, "metadata": meta-info #1, "description": description of model #1}
tool_schema_source.note: Model descriptions gathered from Hugging Face model cards (human-authored).

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: we propose HuggingGPT with an inter-model cooperation protocol
protocol_standardization.note: Proprietary interface; no MCP/A2A mentioned (predates MCP).

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: we use ChatGPT to conduct task planning when receiving a user request, select models according to their function descriptions available in Hugging Face, execute each subtask with the selected AI model, and summarize the response according to the execution results.
loop_primitives.note: Four fixed stages (planning, model selection, execution, response generation); plan-then-execute structure noted, but stage sequence is predetermined. Paper-only evidence.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: the task parsing template comprises four slots ("task", "id", "dep", and "args") to represent the task name, unique identifier, dependencies and arguments

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: an LLM acts as a controller, managing and organizing the cooperation of expert models. The LLM first plans a list of tasks based on the user request and then assigns expert models to each task.
multi_agent_topology.note: Workers are expert ML models, not LLM agents.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: HuggingGPT will automatically feed these task arguments into the models, execute these models to obtain the inference results, and then send them back to the LLM.
delegation_mechanism.note: Delegation is to expert models, not agents; closest value.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: HuggingGPT can autonomously fulfill complex user requests

short_term_state.evidence_quote: we use a unique symbol, “<resource>”, to maintain resource dependencies
short_term_state.note: Task list with ids/deps plus resource table is maintained across stages.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: To assist with task planning, the chat history is available as {{ Chat Logs }}
long_term_memory.note: Chat logs are within-session; no cross-run memory described.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: Instability is mainly caused because LLMs are usually uncontrollable.

self_verification.evidence_quote: we cannot ensure that the generated plan will always be feasible and optimal
self_verification.note: GPT-4 Score is an offline evaluation metric, not a runtime check.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: it still possibly fails to conform to instructions or give incorrect answers during the prediction, leading to exceptions in the program workflow

rollback.evidence_quote: Invoke and execute each selected model, and return the results to ChatGPT.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: After all task executions are completed, HuggingGPT needs to generate the final responses.
termination_condition.note: Run ends when the planned task list is exhausted; no step/cost caps reported.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: This strategy can substantially reduce the token usage in the prompt and effectively select the appropriate models for each task.
cost_controls.note: Top-K candidate filtering reduces tokens but is not a budget/cache/router.

timeouts.evidence_quote: Efficiency poses a common challenge in our framework.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: we offer a hybrid inference endpoint to deploy these models for speedup and computational stability
execution_isolation.note: Hugging Face endpoints plus local endpoints (Fig. 2).

network_policy.note: Remote HF API calls imply network access; no policy described.

permission_model.evidence_quote: HuggingGPT will automatically feed these task arguments into the models, execute these models to obtain the inference results

tracing.evidence_quote: LLM integrates the inference results of experts and generates a summary of workflow logs to respond to the user

replayability.evidence_quote: To enable more stable outputs of LLM, we set the decoding temperature to 0.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: To conduct our evaluation, we invite some annotators to submit some requests. We collect these data as the evaluation dataset.
eval_hooks.note: Evaluation done on an ad-hoc annotated dataset; no built-in runner reported in evidence.

guardrails.evidence_quote: to regulate the LLM output to satisfy the expected format (e.g., JSON format), we set the logit_bias to 0.2 on the format constraints
guardrails.note: Format biasing is not a safety guardrail.

target_domain.evidence_quote: HuggingGPT can tackle a wide range of sophisticated AI tasks spanning different modalities and domains and achieve impressive results in language, vision, speech, and other challenging tasks

open_source.note: Public repo; licence file not in evidence.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: we employed the gpt-3.5-turbo, text-davinci-003 and gpt-4 variants of the GPT models as the main LLMs
model_agnostic.note: Also evaluated with Alpaca-7b and Vicuna-7b as controller.

primary_artifact.evidence_quote: HuggingGPT: Solving AI Tasks with ChatGPT and its Friends in Hugging Face
primary_artifact.note: Coded from the paper; repo not pinned in evidence.

first_release_date.note: Basis: arXiv id 2303.17580 implies v1 late March 2023; no tag information available.
